en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Great Victorious Vajra-Uṣṇīṣa,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India by imperial decree.
At that time, for the sake of all sentient beings in the final age, the World-Honored One manifested five kinds of radiant light.
From the crown of his head, he emits flames of fire that illuminate all the evil demons, spirits, and others within the three realms who do not believe in the Buddha’s teachings,
simultaneously incinerating them all.
When the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi saw this sign,
he addressed the Blessed One, saying:
"The Tathāgata’s fire of wisdom has consumed all those devas, māras, and spirits who cause harm to sentient beings."
Everyone is terrified and finds no peace;
what Dharma do you wish to proclaim?
We only pray that the Tathāgata will expound it for us.
At that time, the Buddha Mahāvairocana addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"There is a vidyārāja named the Great Victorious Uṣṇīṣa Heart Mantra.
By reciting it once, all that is sought shall be fulfilled."
This is the most supreme vidyārāja among all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
If there is one who possesses the vajra-seeds,
they shall recite it fifty thousand times.
All the Buddhas, great Bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, and celestial maidens shall together protect [the practitioner] day and night, causing their aspirations to be fulfilled.
At that time, the Tathāgata spoke these words of illumination:
Oṃ mahāvajraśani hūṃ tarale raḥ phaṭ hūṃ. [Perform] the inner binding with the two hands, bending the ring fingers and thumbs like a crown.
This is called the Fundamental Great Seal (mūlamahāmudrā). If,
during the period when the Final Dharma (paścimakāla) prevails,
there are sentient beings who constantly form this seal and maintain the recitation of the mantra, [they shall attain success].
No military forces can cause them harm;
fire and water cannot burn or drown them;
nor can any evil Māras or malevolent spirits prevail over them.
The holy assembly of the Vajra Womb (Vajradhātu) shall all come to sit and lie down, increasing their protective guardianship.
Furthermore, the method for painting the image is explained:
during the dark fortnight, under the lunar mansion of Bharaṇī, take pure silk cloth.
Paint the Great Victorious Vidyārāja,
wearing a crown of five Buddhas and manifesting twelve arms.
Abiding in the Jñānamuṣṭi-mudrā,
he holds the mudrās of the five-pronged vajra, the blue lotus, the jewel, the *karma*-hook, the noose, the chain, the bell, the sharp sword, and the wheel;
he is established upon a thousand-petaled white lotus.
The color of the body is like white light;
the entire body becomes a mass of fire.
In the four corners, draw the four Vidyārājas.
In the southeast corner, paint Acala-vajra;
in the southwest corner, Hayagrīva-vajra;
and in the northwest corner, Ṣaḍbhuja-vajra.
In the northeast corner, [depict] the Yakṣa Vajra;
draw these four wrathful kings,
each holding their respective weapons and staves.
Manifesting an extremely fierce and powerful majesty,
next draw the celestial kings of the eight directions,
each surrounded by their respective retinues in reverent attendance.
If there is a practitioner of the mantra who wishes to make offerings,
they should do so in a clean room or a quiet place such as a mountain forest,
burning incense and scattering seasonal flowers.
If you recite this mantra five hundred thousand times,
I and the eight Uṣṇīṣas, along with immeasurable devas, bodhisattvas, and vajradevas,
will manifest our forms and constantly serve you according to your wishes.
If there are sentient beings who daily recite and uphold this mantra,
within their present life they shall surpass all devas and humans.
In the final age,
those who hold this seal and mantra shall have bodies like those of the Honored One Samantaprabha.
One will be able to accomplish one billion kinds of aspirations.
Furthermore, if there is a practitioner who performs various rites for subduing Māras and all *avīśas* (obstructive spirits), [they shall succeed].
I shall become ten thousand Vajrakumāras;
thus, may those who maintain this recitation abide forever according to their wishes.
If you have a compassionate heart, do not harbor mutual hatred toward others.
Visualize the syllable HŪṂ upon the heart;
while walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, abide in the samādhi of the deity and accomplish all aspirations.
All sentient beings who behold him will feel joy and love,
thinking of this person as the Vairocana Tathāgata.
Infinite Buddhas constantly come to protect and never abandon them.
The practitioner of the mantra path does not give rise to afflictions such as greed, hatred, or delusion,
and takes deep refuge in the Triple Gem.
Those who dedicate their roots of goodness toward the six realms of existence will surely and swiftly realize unsurpassed bodhi.
The practitioner should empower the five places [of the body] in all impure locations by using the Uṣṇīṣavijaya-vajra mantra and mudrā.
Form a fist with the four fingers of the right hand,
extend the thumb straight upward, and snap the fingers.
The secret mantra is as follows:
